quick.source:
name: quick
description: Make a small change (refactor, docs, chore, a reproduced bug's fix), check and review it, open the draft PR, wait for CI.
start: sync
steps:
  sync:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: implement
      conflict:
        to: sync-resolve
        counter: sync.conflict
  sync-resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: sync
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  implement:
    agent: "Work from what the story already holds: the Plan section of spec.md when a refinement round wrote one, otherwise the issue mirrored in spec.md and its latest `## Triage` comment. Keep to what they ask. A change in behaviour gets a test first; a change to docs or a pure refactor needs none beyond the suite staying green. A bug comes from a reproduce round with a red loop in the handoff's Notes and the issue's latest `## Reproduce` comment: turn it into a failing test at the seam named there before changing any code, then fix the cause. Test your change with `bun packages/cli/src/main.ts …`, never the installed `norn`. Run that dev build only in a throwaway git repo under $TMPDIR, never in this worktree: it is a live norn unit (its .norn-unit marker) and a dev build run there would act on its claim and on its run state (state.json, receipts) in the checkout's machine dir. Run `bun run test` (the unit tier) after each change, and the type check; the integration and e2e tiers run in CI, which the `ci` check waits for, so do not run them before handing back."
    skills:
      - norn-implement
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
      - last_check
      - last_findings
    outcomes:
      done: update
    means:
      done: the change is made; each behaviour change and rework point has a passing test
  update:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: test
      clean: test-merge
      resolved: test-resolution
      conflict:
        to: resolve
        counter: update.conflict
  resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase. When Rework holds the resolution review's findings instead, fix the resolution they name and commit; never rebase."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
      - base_side
    outcomes:
      done: update
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  test:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: review
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  test-merge:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: open-pr
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  test-resolution:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: resolution-review
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  resolution-review:
    agent: "Review only the resolution: each remerge-diff under Inputs is where a merge differs from git's own merge of its parents, a base change the resolver dropped included. Judge whether it keeps the intent of both sides. Report `redescribe` when the merge danger pr.md describes no longer holds."
    skills:
      - norn-review
    inputs:
      - spec
      - resolution
    hand_back:
      changes_requested: findings
    outcomes:
      approve: open-pr
      redescribe: describe
      changes_requested:
        to: resolve
        counter: resolution-review.changes_requested
    means:
      approve: the resolution keeps both sides' intent, no blocking findings; pr.md still describes the merge danger
      redescribe: the resolution is sound, but the merge danger pr.md describes changed
      changes_requested: blocking findings on the resolution in the receipt
  review:
    agent: "Review the change against what the story asks (its Plan, or the issue and its latest triage): it does that and nothing else."
    skills:
      - norn-review
    inputs:
      - spec
      - diff
      - last_findings
    hand_back:
      changes_requested: findings
    outcomes:
      approve: describe
      changes_requested:
        to: implement
        counter: review.changes_requested
    means:
      approve: the change does what the story asks and nothing else, no blocking findings
      changes_requested: blocking findings in the receipt
  describe:
    agent: Write the PR body to pr.md in the spec folder; norn puts the issue link under it.
    skills:
      - norn-pr
    inputs:
      - spec
      - diff
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: open-pr
    means:
      done: "pr.md describes the branch as it is now: summary, evidence, merge danger"
  open-pr:
    open-pr: null
    outcomes:
      done: ci
  ci:
    check: |
      sha=$(gh pr view --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid) || exit 1
      # GitHub starts no CI run on a PR that conflicts with its base: exit 3 is stale, the story
      # updates its branch instead of waiting. UNKNOWN is GitHub still computing: asked again briefly.
      mergeable() {
        m=UNKNOWN
        for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
          m=$(gh pr view --json mergeable -q .mergeable) || return 1
          [ "$m" != UNKNOWN ] && return 0
          sleep 5
        done
      }
      conflicting() { [ "$m" = CONFLICTING ] && echo "PR conflicts with its base: no CI runs on it until the branch takes the base"; }
      mergeable || exit 1
      conflicting && exit 3
      run=
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        run=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --commit "$sha" --event pull_request --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
        [ -n "$run" ] && break
        sleep 10
      done
      if [ -z "$run" ]; then
        mergeable || exit 1
        conflicting && exit 3
        echo "no ci.yml run for $sha after 5m (PR mergeable: $m)"
        exit 1
      fi
      gh run watch "$run" --exit-status --interval 30 >/dev/null && exit 0
      sh .agents/scripts/ci-failures.sh "$run"
      exit 1
    timeout: 30m
    exits:
      "3": stale
    outcomes:
      pass: ready
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: ship.failed
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
  ready:
    gate: Read the draft PR. Approve to wait for the merge (a person merges the PR), or reject with what to change.
    outcomes:
      approve: merge
      reject:
        to: implement
        counter: land.rejected
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
  merge:
    await-merge: null
    outcomes:
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
counters:
  stale_loop:
    max: 10
  sync.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on: sync.done
  update.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on:
      - update.done
      - update.clean
      - update.resolved
  resolution-review.changes_requested:
    max: 2
  review.changes_requested:
    max: 3
  base-update.failed:
    max: 5
  ship.failed:
    max: 3
  land.rejected:
    max: 2
base:
  stale: conflict
  step: update
  verify: test

refinement.source:
name: refinement
description: Agree a story's spec and plan with a person, against the current base; no code.
start: sync
steps:
  sync:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: refine
      conflict:
        to: sync-resolve
        counter: sync.conflict
  sync-resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: sync
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  refine:
    agent: Write the spec into the body of spec.md; keep its frontmatter unchanged.
    skills:
      - norn-refine
    attended: true
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: plan
      questions: clarify
    means:
      done: "spec complete: problem statement, solution, numbered user stories, out of scope; no open questions"
      questions: spec written, but open questions are listed that need the person's answers
  clarify:
    agent: Settle the spec's open questions with the person, one question at a time, folding each answer into the section it changes.
    skills:
      - norn-clarify
    attended: true
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: plan
    means:
      done: every open question is answered and folded into the spec
  plan:
    agent: Write the Plan section of spec.md.
    skills:
      - norn-plan
    attended: true
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: $done
    means:
      done: spec.md's Plan section has seams, a coverage table for every user story, prefactoring, decisions and risks
counters:
  sync.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on: sync.done

release.source:
name: release
description: Write the changelog and propose the version, open the draft PR, wait for its CI, and let a person judge it at ready.
start: prepare
steps:
  prepare:
    agent: "Write the changelog section, the version bumps and the proposed version with its reason as the skill says; a version given in the issue's `## Version` or by the person in Rework wins over your proposal. Also write the PR body to pr.md in the spec folder: the proposed version, its reason and the new changelog section; norn puts the issue link under it. In the same diff as the bump, set `norn_version: X.Y.Z` in .agents/norn.config.yaml by editing the file (not with `norn upgrade`, which runs only in the main checkout) and copy packages/cli/assets/skills/norn* over .agents/skills/norn* as the skill says, so that once the PR merges the published binary is the one main asks for. Rename the issue to \"Release X.Y.Z\" with `gh issue edit`, the one remote write this step allows. Change no code."
    skills:
      - release
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: open-pr
    means:
      done: CHANGELOG.md, packages/cli/package.json, the README badge and norn_version in .agents/norn.config.yaml carry version X.Y.Z, .agents/skills/norn* match the bundled sources; pr.md and the handoff name it with its reason
  update:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: prepare
      conflict:
        to: resolve
        counter: update.conflict
  resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase. CHANGELOG.md and version conflicts: keep the base side; prepare writes the release section again next."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: update
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  open-pr:
    open-pr: null
    outcomes:
      done: ci
  ci:
    check: |
      sha=$(gh pr view --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid) || exit 1
      # GitHub starts no CI run on a PR that conflicts with its base: exit 3 is stale, the story
      # updates its branch instead of waiting. UNKNOWN is GitHub still computing: asked again briefly.

          sleep 5
        done
      }
      conflicting() { [ "$m" = CONFLICTING ] && echo "PR conflicts with its base: no CI runs on it until the branch takes the base"; }
      mergeable || exit 1
      conflicting && exit 3
      run=
      for i in $(seq 1 30); do
        run=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --commit "$sha" --event pull_request --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
        [ -n "$run" ] && break
        sleep 10
      done
      if [ -z "$run" ]; then
        mergeable || exit 1
        conflicting && exit 3
        echo "no ci.yml run for $sha after 5m (PR mergeable: $m)"
        exit 1
      fi
      gh run watch "$run" --exit-status --interval 30 >/dev/null && exit 0
      sh .agents/scripts/ci-failures.sh "$run"
      exit 1
    timeout: 30m
    exits:
      "3": stale
    outcomes:
      pass: ready
      fail: $stuck
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
  ready:
    gate: "Read the draft release PR: the proposed version and its reason, and the new CHANGELOG.md section. Approve to wait for the merge (a person merges the PR; CI then tags and publishes), or reject with the version or changelog changes you want."
    outcomes:
      approve: merge
      reject:
        to: prepare
        counter: ready.reject
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
  merge:
    await-merge: null
    outcomes:
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
counters:
  stale_loop:
    max: 10
  update.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on: update.done
  ready.reject:
    max: 2
base:
  stale: behind

reproduce.source:
# Reproduce workflow — repo-local copy of the shipped one (label norn:wf:reproduce, set by
# the bug report template and the `issue` skill). An unattended agent follows the report through the
# real interface, builds a loop that goes red on the symptom, minimises it, confirms the cause and
# names the seam for a regression test. It posts all of that as an issue comment and changes no code.
# Every outcome ends the round ($done): the fix is a quick round (`norn story edit gh-N --workflow
# quick`), whose implement turns the red loop into a failing test first.
name: reproduce
description: Reproduce a bug through the real interface, confirm its cause and the seam for a regression test; change no code.
start: reproduce
steps:
  reproduce:
    agent: >-
      The issue is mirrored in spec.md; read its comments too. First follow the report as a user, through
      the real interface (`bun packages/cli/src/main.ts …` after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, never the installed
      `norn`), and record what you saw. Run that dev build only in a throwaway git repo under $TMPDIR, never in this worktree: it is a live norn unit (its .norn-unit marker) and a dev build run there would act on its claim and on its run state (state.json, receipts) in the checkout's machine dir. Then build a loop
      that goes red on that exact symptom, minimise it and confirm the cause. You are told not to fix:
      change no file, spec.md included, but the handoff.
      Post the findings as an issue comment that starts with `## Reproduce` (`## Reproduce (updated)` on a rerun):
      the loop command, the minimised repro, what it prints, the confirmed cause (`file:line`, or the ranked
      hypotheses left) and the seam for a regression test. That one comment is the only remote write this
      step allows, an exception to the brief's rule on remote writes; never edit the issue, label, assign or close.
      Write the same under Notes in the handoff (the next agent does not see your Resume); a long loop output goes in evidence, with a pointer.
    skills: [norn-diagnose]
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    outcomes:
      reproduced:       $done
      cannot_reproduce: $done
    means:
      reproduced: "the bug was observed as a user and a loop goes red on it; loop, repro, cause and seam posted and in the handoff"
      cannot_reproduce: "followed the report faithfully and the bug did not occur, nor in any loop tried; what was tried posted and in the handoff"

slice.source:
name: slice
description: Build one slice test-first, check and review it, and integrate it into the story branch.
start: implement
steps:
  implement:
    agent: "Build this slice test-first: each acceptance criterion in the slice file, or each rework point from a red check or a review, ends with a passing test. Stay inside the slice; later slices have their own steps. Run `bun run test` (the unit tier) after each change, and the type check; this slice's `test` check runs only those two: the integration and e2e tiers run in CI, once the story's PR is open, so do not run them before handing back."
    skills:
      - norn-implement
    inputs:
      - slice
      - spec
      - handoff
      - last_check
      - last_findings
    outcomes:
      done: test
    means:
      done: every acceptance criterion (or rework point) has a passing test
  test:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: review
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: test.fail
  review:
    agent: Review this slice's diff against its acceptance criteria and the spec, before it integrates into the story branch.
    skills:
      - norn-review
    inputs:
      - slice
      - spec
      - diff
      - last_findings
    hand_back:
      changes_requested: findings
    outcomes:
      approve: integrate
      changes_requested:
        to: implement
        counter: review.changes_requested
    means:
      approve: all criteria met, no blocking findings
      changes_requested: blocking findings in the receipt
  integrate:
    integrate: null
    outcomes:
      done: $done
      conflict:
        to: merge
        counter: integrate.conflict
  merge:
    agent: "Integrating this slice into the story branch conflicted: resolve each conflict keeping the intent of both sides, and prove it with the tests."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - slice
      - spec
    outcomes:
      done: integrate
    means:
      done: conflicts resolved keeping the intent of both sides; tests pass
counters:
  test.fail:
    max: 5
  integrate.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on: integrate.done
  review.changes_requested:
    max: 3

story.source:
name: story
description: Slice a planned story against the current base, run the slices, verify the story, open the draft PR, wait for CI.
start: sync
steps:
  sync:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: slice
      conflict:
        to: sync-resolve
        counter: sync.conflict
  sync-resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
    outcomes:
      done: sync
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  slice:
    agent: "Write slice files to slices/<nn>-<slug>.md in the spec folder. A slice has no QA of its own: list every slice's criteria in spec.md's frontmatter `criteria` too, each id prefixed with its slice number (`01.AC1`), next to the story's own, so the story's QA gives each one a verdict. First check the Plan section of spec.md against the code on this base: when spec.md has no Plan section, or the base changed what the plan relies on so that it no longer holds, write no slice files, say what no longer holds in the handoff's Notes and report `replan`."
    skills:
      - norn-slice
    inputs:
      - spec
      - slices
    outcomes:
      done: approve-slices
      replan: $stuck
    means:
      done: slice files written against the current base; every user story is covered by some slice's acceptance
      replan: "spec.md has no Plan, or the base no longer fits it: what no longer holds is in the handoff; the person replans with `norn story edit <story> --workflow refinement --at plan`"
  approve-slices:
    gate: Review the slice files in the spec folder (edit them if needed). Approve to start the slices, or reject with what to change.
    outcomes:
      approve: slices
      reject:
        to: slice
        counter: approve-slices.reject
  slices:
    slices: null
    outcomes:
      done: update
      stuck: $stuck
  update:
    update-branch: null
    outcomes:
      done: test
      clean: test-merge
      resolved: test-resolution
      conflict:
        to: resolve
        counter: update.conflict
  resolve:
    agent: "Base mode: merge the base commit named in Rework into the story branch in this worktree, resolve, commit the merge; never rebase. When Rework holds the resolution review's findings instead, fix the resolution they name and commit; never rebase."
    skills:
      - norn-merge
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
      - base_side
    outcomes:
      done: update
    means:
      done: base merged into the story branch, conflicts resolved and committed
  test:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: qa
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  test-merge:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: open-pr
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  test-resolution:
    check: bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run test && bun run typecheck
    timeout: 15m
    outcomes:
      pass: resolution-review
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: base-update.failed
  resolution-review:
    agent: "Review only the resolution: each remerge-diff under Inputs is where a merge differs from git's own merge of its parents, a base change the resolver dropped included. Judge whether it keeps the intent of both sides. Report `redescribe` when the merge danger pr.md describes no longer holds."
    skills:
      - norn-review
    inputs:
      - spec
      - resolution
    hand_back:
      changes_requested: findings
    outcomes:
      approve: open-pr
      redescribe: describe
      changes_requested:
        to: resolve
        counter: resolution-review.changes_requested
    means:
      approve: the resolution keeps both sides' intent, no blocking findings; pr.md still describes the merge danger
      redescribe: the resolution is sound, but the merge danger pr.md describes changed
      changes_requested: blocking findings on the resolution in the receipt
  qa:
    agent: The criteria are spec.md's frontmatter `criteria`; an id `<nn>.<id>` is criterion `<id>` of slice file `<nn>-*.md`, which says what it means.
    skills:
      - norn-qa
    inputs:
      - spec
      - slices
      - diff
    criteria: required
    hand_back:
      fail: findings
    outcomes:
      pass: describe
      fail:
        to: implement
        counter: qa_loop
      partial: human-qa
      unverified: human-qa
    means:
      pass: every acceptance criterion of the story and its slices observed with evidence
      fail: a criterion fails; repro in findings
      partial: criteria only a person can judge, evidence prepared
      unverified: criteria this session could not check; how to check each one is in the report
    verdict:
      pass: pass
      fail: fail
      partial: person
      unverified: unverified
  human-qa:
    gate: Check the criteria QA could not settle (listed with how to check each). Approve, or reject with what failed.
    outcomes:
      approve: describe
      reject:
        to: implement
        counter: qa_loop
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
  implement:
    agent: Run `bun run test` (the unit tier) after each change, and the type check; the integration and e2e tiers run in CI, which the `ci` check waits for, so do not run them before handing back.
    skills:
      - norn-implement
    inputs:
      - spec
      - handoff
      - last_check
      - last_findings
    outcomes:
      done: review
    means:
      done: every rework point has a passing test

    agent: "Review the story-level rework against the findings it answers and the spec: it fixes what they ask and nothing else."

  describe:

    skills:

    inputs:

        [ -n "$run" ] && break
        sleep 10
      done
      if [ -z "$run" ]; then
        mergeable || exit 1
        conflicting && exit 3

        exit 1
      fi

    outcomes:

        counter: stale_loop
  merge:
    await-merge: null
    outcomes:
      stale:
        to: update
        counter: stale_loop
counters:
  qa_loop:
    max: 2
  stale_loop:
    max: 10
  sync.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on: sync.done
  approve-slices.reject:
    max: 3
  update.conflict:
    max: 2
    reset_on:
      - update.done
      - update.clean
      - update.resolved
  resolution-review.changes_requested:
    max: 2
  review.changes_requested:
    max: 3
  base-update.failed:
    max: 5
  ship.failed:
    max: 3
  land.rejected:
    max: 2
base:
  stale: conflict
  step: update
  verify: test

triage.source:
# Triage workflow — repo-local copy of the shipped one, norn's own default (config
# `workflow`: triage), for stories and features; a bug starts in `reproduce` instead (label
# norn:wf:reproduce). An unattended agent checks the issue still holds, posts its findings as an issue
# comment (spec.md stays as intake wrote it): the recommendation lives only there, the outcome is plain
# `done`. That ends the round ($done): the person starts the next one (`norn story edit gh-N --workflow
# refinement|quick|reproduce`) or closes the issue. Agents never run it.
name: triage
description: Check an issue still holds, add its context, and recommend what comes next (refinement, quick, reproduce) or closing it.
start: explore
steps:
  explore:
    agent: >-
      The issue is mirrored in spec.md. Run norn's behaviour from this checkout's code, `bun packages/cli/src/main.ts …`
      after `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, never the installed `norn`, and only in a throwaway git repo under $TMPDIR:
      this worktree is a live norn unit. A change to norn's
      documented behaviour is a `refinement`, unless the change is small and settled. Post the `## Triage` comment on it and add the kind, risk and priority
      labels: `norn:kind:bug|feature|security|chore|docs`, `norn:risk:low|medium|high`,
      `norn:priority:low|medium|high|extreme`; a label missing on the remote is named in the comment with
      "norn upgrade creates it". That comment and those labels are the only remote writes this step allows,
      an exception to the brief's rule on remote writes; never remove a label, the intake label `norn` included. Change no file, spec.md included,
      but the handoff. The recommendation lives only in that comment:
      report `norn done done --handoff "<recommendation>: <reason>"`.
    skills: [norn-triage]
    inputs: [spec, handoff]
    outcomes:
      done: $done
    means:
      done: "the ## Triage comment is posted, with one recommendation (refinement, quick, reproduce or close) and its reason, and the kind, risk and priority labels that could be set are on the issue"
